headline: Approved a Vote Mob at the Farmers Market to encourage online voting for its Farmland Trust People's Choice award.
summary: Members discussed a Cash Mob for the Farmers Market. Market leaders proposed a Vote Mob instead, to encourage online votes for the market's People's Choice award from Farmland Trust, with voting running through September 30, 2026. Members voted to hold the Vote Mob at the Farmers Market on September 19, 2026.
decisions: Approved running a Vote Mob at the Farmers Market on September 19, 2026; all present voted in favor.

decision_titles: Vote Mob event at the Farmers Market on September 19, 2026
plain_text:
Diversity Council Special Meeting 
Tuesday, August 18, 2026 at 7:15pm 
Meeting Room 1-2, City Hall, 111 N. Main Street & on Zoom 
 
Present:  Interim Chair Marcus Patton, Council Members Sandy Kamens, David 
Rackliffe, Carolyn Palmquist, Danny Palmquist, and Tony Lopes (Zoom) 
Absent: Council Member Jeff Israel 
Guests: Dawn Nielsen, Chair of the Board of Directors for the Bristol Farmers Market 
  Mickey Goldwasser, Director of the Bristol Farmers Market 
 
I. Call to Order 
The Interim Chair called the meeting to order at 7:17pm. Council Members and 
guests introduced themselves. There was a quorum. 
 
II. Farmers Market Cash Mob Discussion and Brainstorming 
A. Review of the Cash Mob Objectives 
--Examples of Previous Cash Mob executions 
The Interim Chair provided a brief history of the revived Cash Mob the Diversity 
Council as it has recently been operating. Details included the voting process 
and event planning and completion. The idea of focusing on farms for the next 
Cash Mob came up at an earlier Diversity Council meeting, which transitioned 
into the idea of holding the Cash Mob on an existing Farmers Market date, which 
led to the initial contact with Mickey Goldwasser of the Farmers Market.  
 
B. Review of the Farmers Market 
--Farmers Market representatives discuss different registered vendors 
Dawn Nielsen provided an update on the current success of this year’s Farmers 
Market including receiving various grant funds to support their efforts as a not-
for-profit entity. These grants allow for programs like Double SNAP Benefits. The 
market is now being held at 18 Main Street in the parking lot of Express Kitchens 
who is the market’s Premiere Sponsor. The new location has expanded the 
vending and parking spaces which has added to the market’s success. Many of 
the vendors report selling out each week. 
 
The Farmers Market Board was grateful to be considered for the next Cash Mob 
in support of their vendors. As the goal of a Cash Mob is to infuse cash sales and
support to a local business, and with the market doing so well with a large 
amount of community support already, the Farmers Market Board feels the 
Cash Mob would be of better benefit to one of the city’s businesses. Dawn and 
Mickey expressed their desire to share the Cash Mob benefit to an area business 
that might need the exposure more than the market. 
 
C. How to Drive Attendance to the Farmers Market 
--Assortment of ideas that Diversity Council members can execute and 
advertise to attract shoppers to the Cash Mob 
--Farmers Market representative’s guidance on possibilities 
Dawn Nielsen presented an alternative to the Cash Mob which would still allow 
the Council to provide support to the Farmers Market and keep the Cash Mob 
movement for an area business. The proposed action is to encourage the online 
voting for the market through a People’s Choice award provided through 
Farmland Trust.  
 
Farmland Trust recognizes markets across the country (nationally, regionally 
and by state). Voting is allowed as one vote per person per email address. The 
goal of the Bristol Farmers Market for 2026 is to be voted #1. Currently they are 
at #2 behind the Coventry Farmers Market. Discussion followed, including 
creating this as a Vote Mob. Voting runs through September 30, 2026. The 
winner receives bragging rights and recognition across the farmers market 
community, as well as online and the various national, regional and state levels. 
 
D. Date Selection of the Farmers Market Cash Mob event 
Discussion continued, including the Diversity Council being a featured non-
profit at an existing market day to create a Vote Mob Event. Council Members 
would open the market, share a few words about their mission, and be there 
through the day to actively encourage attendees to vote. Additional promotion 
would begin through the Council’s social media beforehand. Dawn noted that 
voting is on the honor system and no offers or incentives to vote could be given, 
to which the Council was in agreement. September 19, 2026 was proposed as 
the Vote Mob Event date, and event logistics were reviewed. 
 
With no further discussion noted, the Interim Chair made the following Motion: 
 
Motion for the Diversity Council to run the Vote Mob at the Farmers Market on 
September 19, 2026.
The motion was seconded by Council Member Kamens. All were in favor and the 
motion was accepted into the record. 
 
III. Adjournment 
With the Special Meeting business completed, the Interim Chair adjourned the 
meeting at 7:50pm 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
Sharon Arsego 
Recording Secretary
